blocks.name: Bauxite Ore
blocks.desc: Reddish ore found between Y 0 and Y 64, in veins of up to seven blocks. Mine it with a stone pickaxe or better for Raw Bauxite; Fortune increases the drop and Silk Touch keeps the ore.

blocks.name: Uranium Ore
blocks.desc: Faintly glowing ore found deep down, from Y -64 to Y 16, in small veins. Mine it with an iron pickaxe for Raw Uranium (Fortune helps, Silk Touch keeps the ore). Raw Uranium can't be smelted: it goes to a Uranium Mill, two to a Yellowcake, and a Fuel Cell takes twelve.

blocks.name: Steel Block
blocks.desc: Compact storage for nine Steel Ingots. Heavy builds such as the Core Router, Modular Reactor and Quantum Core use it as a structural frame.

blocks.name: Raised Floor Tile
blocks.desc: A perforated floor panel that blocks airflow. Use it to seal the floor between hot and cold aisles so rack exhaust cannot creep back into the intakes.

blocks.name: Blanking Panel
blocks.desc: Seals gaps in a row of racks. Like the raised floor, it blocks airflow, which keeps hot exhaust air out of the cold aisle.

blocks.name: Power Cable
blocks.desc: Links generators, batteries, PDUs and loads into one power network. Every machine touching the same connected cable run shares power. Cable cut events sever a segment; right-click it with a Repair Kit to splice it.

blocks.name: Diesel Generator
blocks.desc: Backup generator that delivers 40 kW. It spins up only when demand exceeds solar, wind, reactor and utility supply, and takes 10 seconds to get there. It burns any furnace fuel plus Rackcraft fuels from its slot, only while it is actually supplying power. Open it to watch its output, fuel and spin-up live; it smokes while running and vents 4 kW of heat out of its radiator at the back.

blocks.name: Solar Panel
blocks.desc: Produces up to 4 kW in daylight when the block above it can see the sky. Output scales with sky light. A solar panel is the first source drawn on in any network.

blocks.name: Wind Turbine
blocks.desc: Produces up to 8 kW depending on altitude. It runs at 25% at Y 70 or below and reaches full output at Y 130. Thunderstorms add another 50%.

blocks.name: Power Distribution Unit
blocks.desc: A distribution point on the power network. Open it to see draw and satisfaction, and use Reset Breaker to clear a tripped breaker.

blocks.name: Server Rack
blocks.desc: The heart of the facility, with eight module bays: any module fits any bay, one per bay, so a rack takes eight GPU Blades as happily as eight Pi Nodes. Air comes in the front and every kilowatt it draws comes out as heat: out of the back as hot air, or, for liquid-cooled modules, 85% of it down its coolant pipe. A rack mines RackCoin (RC) when powered, networked by fiber to a router, and kept cool. Its screen shows the live mining rate or exactly what is stopping it, and where its heat is going. Use the 25/50/75/100% buttons to cap its load.

blocks.name: Exhaust Fan
blocks.desc: Pulls hot air out of the block in front of it and dumps it outside: up to 10 kW, only while that air is at least 1 C above ambient, so it idles (and stays clean) when there's nothing to move. Point it into a hot aisle. Moving heat outside makes smog in proportion to the heat moved; smog spreads to neighbouring chunks and dims solar panels, and past 30 it makes you dizzy, then come spells of blindness, a hacking cough, and from 70 poison. Wear a Respirator or run a Smog Scrubber. Draws 0.2 kW.

blocks.name: Coolant Pipe
blocks.desc: Each connected run of Coolant Pipe is one coolant loop. Heat goes in from racks with liquid-cooled modules, Rear-Door Coolers, CRAC units and Modular Reactors, and comes out at heat sinks: Cooling Towers, Dry Coolers, Chillers and Water Heat Exchangers. Run it as far as you like, so the heat can be dumped well away from the racks. Check a loop with the Multimeter: heat in versus what its sinks can take.

blocks.name: Cooling Tower
blocks.desc: Heat sink for a coolant loop. It takes 120 kW of heat out of the loop when a Freshwater Pump on the same loop supplies it 4 units of water, and only 20 kW dry. It drinks the lake: the water it uses drains source blocks from the pump's shore. Draws 4 kW.

blocks.name: CRAC Unit
blocks.desc: Computer-room air conditioner: takes heat out of the room air and puts it into its coolant loop. It pulls up to 40 kW from the air on each of its front and back faces, more the hotter that air is. Its loop needs sinks to take that heat. Draws 3 kW.

blocks.name: Rear-Door Cooler
blocks.desc: A radiator door for the back of a rack. Place it against a rack's back face and it catches up to 40 kW of the rack's hot exhaust and puts it into its coolant loop instead of the room; anything left comes out of its far side. The simplest way to keep a big rack from cooking its neighbours. Draws 0.3 kW.

blocks.name: Dry Cooler
blocks.desc: Heat sink for a coolant loop that needs no water: big fans blow outside air across a radiator. It takes 40 kW out of the loop in temperate biomes, 60 kW in snowy ones and only 24 kW in deserts, savannas and badlands. Draws 2 kW.

blocks.name: Chiller
blocks.desc: Heavy-duty heat sink for a coolant loop: takes 250 kW out of the loop anywhere, indoors or out, with no water. It pays for it in power: 5 kW plus a fifth of the heat it moves (50 kW more at full tilt).

blocks.name: Water Heat Exchanger
blocks.desc: Heat sink for a coolant loop that dumps heat into a body of water: place it touching water and it takes 3 kW per water source block within four blocks, up to 120 kW. Sea water works, and the water is never used up. Draws 0.5 kW.

blocks.name: Battery Bank
blocks.desc: Stores 3,000 kJ of surplus power, charging at up to 15 kW and discharging at up to 60 kW; it loses 10% of the energy going in and 10% coming out. Build Battery Banks into a solid cube, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5, and they form a Grid-Scale Battery: one store holding every bank's charge and charging and discharging at every bank's rate, with 10% more capacity per bank for each step up in size (40% more in a 5-cube) and smaller losses, 8% each way for a 2-cube down to 2% for a 5-cube.

blocks.name: Utility Intake
blocks.desc: A grid connection supplying 100 kW of steady power. It drops to zero during a Utility Outage event, so pair it with batteries and diesel backup.

blocks.name: Fiber Cable
blocks.desc: Connects racks to routers, controllers and monitoring walls. Racks only earn credits over fiber that reaches a router.

blocks.name: Item Pipe
blocks.desc: Moves items between storage and the machines that use them. Connect Storage Arrays or Tape Libraries to Kids' Art Tables, Scriptorium Desks, Diesel Generators and Modular Reactors: once a second they are topped up from storage (paper, crayons, ink, fuel, Fuel Cells) and finished Art Aggregates and Text Corpora go back in. It is its own network, separate from fiber.

blocks.name: Uplink Router
blocks.desc: Provides 100 units of bandwidth to its fiber network. A rack needs bandwidth equal to its mining rate in RC/s; with less, earnings are scaled down proportionally.

blocks.name: Core Router
blocks.desc: A backbone router that provides 1,000 units of bandwidth, enough for a full hall of GPU blades and quantum cores.

blocks.name: Facility Controller
blocks.desc: The operations desk. It shows credits, availability, the active contract and any running event, and sells parts for RackCoin. Players within 64 blocks of a controller are alerted when an event starts.

blocks.name: Coolant Distribution Unit
blocks.desc: Delivers liquid cooling directly to hardware. A Quantum Core only runs in a rack that has a CDU directly beside it. Draws 0.5 kW and sits on the coolant loop like a pipe.

blocks.name: Modular Reactor
blocks.desc: A small modular reactor: 500 kW of steady power, burning one Fuel Cell every 30 minutes at full output (less at part load), and every spent cell comes out as Spent Fuel in its waste slot. Build reactors into a solid cube, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5, and they form one reactor array: the casing changes to show it, the output of every core adds up, fuel and waste are shared evenly across every core's slots, and each core burns 5% (2-cube) up to 20% (5-cube) less fuel. When the waste slots are full the reactor stops: seal the Spent Fuel into casks. Its heat, 30% of its output, goes into its coolant loop if piped, otherwise into the air.

blocks.name: Uranium Mill
blocks.desc: Grinds and leaches Raw Uranium into Yellowcake: two ore make one. Like every nuclear machine it is a multiblock: build Uranium Mills into a solid cube, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5, to make it work at all. Every block in the cube is a core: each core finishes one batch every 30 seconds and draws 20 kW while working, and bigger cubes use up to 20% less power per core. Inputs are shared evenly across the cube; feed and empty it from any block, by hand, hopper or Item Pipe.

blocks.name: Gas Centrifuge
blocks.desc: Enriches uranium: spins six Yellowcake into one Enriched Uranium and four Depleted Uranium, two minutes per batch per core, 60 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5 Gas Centrifuges (a real cascade, and a real power bill).

blocks.name: Fuel Fabricator
blocks.desc: The only way to make Fuel Cells: one Enriched Uranium and two Steel Ingots make one cell, a minute per batch per core, 30 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5.

blocks.name: Cask Sealer
blocks.desc: Seals nuclear waste away for good: four Spent Fuel and four Depleted Uranium (the shielding) make one Sealed Waste Cask, a minute per batch per core, 15 kW per working core. A multiblock: build a solid cube of 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5.

blocks.name: Sealed Waste Cask
blocks.desc: Four Spent Fuel rods sealed behind steel and depleted uranium. Completely safe to carry, stack and store: line them up on a concrete pad somewhere and try not to think about the next ten thousand years.

blocks.name: Monitoring Wall
blocks.desc: A wall display for the fiber network. Open it to see facility power, the hottest inlet and total load.

blocks.name: Fire Suppression Tank
blocks.desc: Holds a Suppression Canister in its single slot, ready for the facility's fire protection.

blocks.name: Crypto Exchange
blocks.desc: Spend the RackCoin your racks have mined. Pick a tab, then click an offer to buy it; Shift-click buys ten. The screen shows your balance and live mining rate, and hovering an offer you can't afford yet tells you how long until you can. It needs no power or cables: every rack in the world pays into one shared balance.

blocks.name: Storage Array
blocks.desc: Eight bays for Storage Drives. Like a rack it needs power (0.4 kW plus 0.15 kW per drive), takes cool air in the front and exhausts heat out the back. Link it to a Storage Terminal with Fiber Cable. If it loses power or reaches 40 C, its drives go offline until fixed; nothing is lost.

blocks.name: Tape Library
blocks.desc: Cold storage. Holds four Tape Cartridges of a million items each and draws only 0.3 kW. Items on tape take two seconds to mount before they reach your inventory. When your drives pass 85% full, the items you have not used for longest are archived to tape automatically.

blocks.name: Storage Terminal
blocks.desc: Your window into storage on the same fiber network. Search, take and deposit items; craft on the 3x3 grid, which refills itself from storage; encode Recipe Patterns; and start autocrafting jobs. Ctrl-click a craftable item (marked +) to choose how many to make.

blocks.name: Wireless Transmitter
blocks.desc: Lets a Wireless Terminal reach this fiber network. Range starts at 16 blocks. Upgrade it in its screen with RackCoin or with resources: up to 1,024 blocks, then unlimited in this dimension, then every dimension. Each level doubles its power draw.

blocks.name: Freshwater Pump
blocks.desc: Supplies fresh water to the Cooling Towers on its coolant loop. Place it touching a lake or river; ocean and beach water is salt and won't do. It draws 1.5 kW and supplies one unit per three water source blocks within six blocks, up to 16 units: four towers' worth. It drinks the lake: every four minutes of one unit drains a source block from the shore. Only towers need water; Dry Coolers, Chillers and Water Heat Exchangers don't.

blocks.name: Kids' Art Table
blocks.desc: Training data for the image model. Stock it with paper and Crayons and baby villagers come running to draw. Each kid finishes a drawing every 20 seconds (up to four kids); four drawings make a Crayon Art Aggregate. Kids at a stocked table never seem to grow up. Connect it to a Storage Array with Item Pipe and it restocks itself and sends the aggregates back to storage; hoppers work too.

blocks.name: Scriptorium Desk
blocks.desc: Training data for the language model. Use Shackles on a librarian within six blocks to chain them to the desk, then stock it with paper and ink sacs. The librarian writes a Librarian Text Corpus every 30 seconds from two paper; an ink sac lasts four. Connect it to a Storage Array with Item Pipe and it restocks itself and files the corpora in storage. They can't leave and complain about it constantly. Sneak-right-click them with an empty hand to set them free.

blocks.name: Operations Terminal
blocks.desc: Runs the whole facility from one screen: the AI contract board (accept, pick a model, generate, deliver), what every cluster of racks is doing and its policy, the model lineup and each model's training, RackCoin income, and every problem with racks, storage, pumps, cables, generators and smog in this dimension. It needs no power or cables.

blocks.name: Smog Scrubber
blocks.desc: Pulls smog back out of the air: at full power it removes 1.5 smog per second from its own chunk and 0.75 from each neighbouring chunk. It draws 6 kW, so it is cheaper than the poison. Place it near your exhaust fans.

blocks.name: Creative Power Source
blocks.desc: Creative only. Supplies as much power as you set, forever, to the power network it touches. Right-click to set the output in kW (needs creative mode or operator).

blocks.name: Creative Rack
blocks.desc: Creative only. Mines RackCoin at the rate you set, with no modules, power, fiber or cooling needed. It can also draw a set load from its power network, which makes it a test load for generators. Right-click to set both values.

blocks.name: Creative Cooler
blocks.desc: Creative only. Holds the air cells in front of and behind it at the temperature you set, regardless of how much heat is dumped there. Air never goes below the ambient temperature (24 C by default). Right-click to set the target in C.

blocks.name: Creative Router
blocks.desc: Creative only. Gives its fiber network as much bandwidth as you set. Right-click to change it.

blocks.name: Block of Coke
blocks.desc: Nine pieces of coke pressed into a block. It burns for 1,600 seconds in a Diesel Generator, the longest-lasting fuel in the mod.

items.name: Rackcraft Field Manual
items.desc: This book. Right-click it to open. Click any Rackcraft ingredient in a recipe to jump to its page.

items.name: Raw Bauxite
items.desc: Unrefined aluminium ore. Smelt it in a furnace, or twice as fast in a blast furnace, to get Aluminum Ingots.

items.name: Aluminum Ingot
items.desc: A light metal used for coolant pipes, fans, solar frames and cryogenic parts.

items.name: Steel Ingot
items.desc: Iron refined in a blast furnace. It forms the chassis of nearly every machine.

items.name: Silicon
items.desc: Blast Nether Quartz to make it, or recycle a Failed Module. It is the base material for every chip.

items.name: Copper Wire
items.desc: One copper ingot makes six wires. Wire goes into circuit boards, scanners and repair kits.

items.name: Circuit Board
items.desc: The universal electronics component used by almost every machine and module.

items.name: CPU Chip
items.desc: A general-purpose processor. Two CPUs make a GPU chip.

items.name: RAM Module
items.desc: Memory for servers and GPU blades. Each one needs a gold ingot.

items.name: GPU Chip
items.desc: A diamond-tipped parallel processor for GPU blades, quantum cores and core routers.

items.name: Cryo Coil
items.desc: An aluminium coil packed in blue ice that keeps a Quantum Core near absolute zero.

items.name: Pi Node
items.desc: A starter module. It draws 0.05 to 0.15 kW and mines 0.5 RC per second at full load.

items.name: 1U Server
items.desc: A workhorse module. It draws 0.2 to 0.6 kW and mines 2 RC per second at full load.

items.name: GPU Blade
items.desc: An accelerator card. It draws 1 to 3 kW and mines 12 RC per second at full load. Plan for its heat. Water-cooled: it needs 2 units from a Freshwater Pump. It also lends 10 AI compute to contract work, which pays a little better than mining.

items.name: ASIC Miner
items.desc: A module built only to mine crypto. It draws 0.4 to 1.2 kW and mines 5 RC per second at full load, cheap for what it earns, but it runs hot. Like all tier 3 hardware it is water-cooled: it needs a Freshwater Pump on its rack's coolant network (1 unit).

items.name: Quantum Core
items.desc: The endgame module. It draws 3 to 9 kW and mines 60 RC per second, but only runs when a CDU is directly beside its rack. On top of its CDU it needs 4 units of freshwater cooling from a pump.

items.name: Tensor Accelerator
items.desc: An AI card. It can't mine, but it lends 12 AI compute to contract generation and model training, which pays about a third more than a GPU Blade mining in the same bay. It draws 0.8 to 2.6 kW and needs freshwater cooling (2 units).

items.name: Crafting Coprocessor
items.desc: A rack module built for autocrafting: 8 general compute (four 1U Servers' worth) for 0.9 kW, and air-cooled, so it needs no coolant loop. It can't mine, and lends only 0.5 AI compute. Racks full of them turn a Storage Terminal's job queue into a production line. Boots in 4 seconds.

items.name: Crafting Accelerator
items.desc: The heavy autocrafting module: 30 general compute (five GPU Blades' worth) for 3.5 kW. It is liquid-cooled, so its rack must be on a coolant loop with a heat sink. It can't mine and lends only 2 AI compute. Boots in 8 seconds.

items.name: Failed Module
items.desc: Dead hardware. Recycle it in a blast furnace to recover Silicon.

items.name: Thermal Scanner
items.desc: Hold it to see coloured heat particles in every warm air cell within 24 blocks: blue is cool and red is past 40 C. Right-click a rack while holding it to read the inlet and exhaust temperatures.

items.name: Multimeter
items.desc: Right-click any machine or cable for a live readout: power delivered against demand, generator fuel, battery charge, rack mining status, and fiber bandwidth. Sneak-right-click a machine to rotate it.

items.name: Repair Kit
items.desc: Right-click a cut cable to splice it back together. Each kit holds 8 repairs.

items.name: Fuel Cell
items.desc: The fuel for the Modular Reactor: one cell runs a reactor for 30 minutes at full output and leaves a Spent Fuel rod behind. It can't be crafted or bought: a Fuel Fabricator makes it from Enriched Uranium. Item Pipes can deliver them from storage.

items.name: Suppression Canister
items.desc: A pressurised extinguishing agent that is loaded into a Fire Suppression Tank.

items.name: 1K Storage Drive
items.desc: Hot storage for 1,024 items of any mix of types. Goes in a Storage Array. Its contents stay with the drive, so you can move it to another array.

items.name: 4K Storage Drive
items.desc: Hot storage for 4,096 items.

items.name: 16K Storage Drive
items.desc: Hot storage for 16,384 items.

items.name: 64K Storage Drive
items.desc: Hot storage for 65,536 items.

items.name: Tape Cartridge
items.desc: Cold storage for 1,048,576 items. Goes in a Tape Library. Cheap and huge, but players wait two seconds for each read.

items.name: Blank Pattern
items.desc: Put one in the Storage Terminal's pattern slot, lay out a recipe on the crafting grid, and press Encode to make a Recipe Pattern.

items.name: Recipe Pattern
items.desc: An encoded crafting recipe. Store it anywhere in the network and its output becomes autocraftable; the planner chains patterns together for multi-step recipes.

items.name: Wireless Terminal
items.desc: A Storage Terminal in your pocket. Sneak-right-click a Wireless Transmitter to link it, then right-click anywhere in range. Beyond its range or in another dimension it needs an upgraded transmitter.

items.name: Coke
items.desc: Coal or charcoal baked in a blast furnace. It burns twice as long as coal: 160 seconds of diesel runtime.

items.name: Biomass Pellet
items.desc: Compressed crop waste. Eight crops, seeds, leaves or saplings plus bone meal make four pellets, which each burn for 40 seconds. It is a renewable fuel for farms.

items.name: Biodiesel Canister
items.desc: Refined biomass in an aluminium can. It runs a Diesel Generator for 8 minutes, the best renewable fuel for backup power.

items.name: Crayons
items.desc: A box of wax crayons for the Kids' Art Table. Lasts 64 drawings.

items.name: Shackles
items.desc: Use on a librarian near a free Scriptorium Desk to chain them to it. You can see the chain from their wrists to the desk. Only librarians can write.

items.name: Crayon Art Aggregate
items.desc: Four children's drawings, scanned and tagged. Upload it to one of the image models (SketchDiffusion, Nano Melon, Nano Melon Pro) at an Operations Terminal.

items.name: Librarian Text Corpus
items.desc: Several thousand words a librarian really didn't want to write. Upload it to one of the Gemerald language models (Flash-Lite, Flash, Pro) at an Operations Terminal.

items.name: Generated Image
items.desc: An AI-generated image, made for a contract. It remembers its prompt and quality: keep spares, because clients often ask for the same thing again.

items.name: Generated Document
items.desc: AI-generated writing: essays, homework, legal documents and worse. It remembers its prompt and quality, so a spare can fill a repeat order.

items.name: Respirator
items.desc: A half-face mask with charcoal filters, worn in the helmet slot. While you wear it smog can't touch you: no dizziness, blindness, cough or poison. The filter clogs in smog (about 40 minutes of it, faster when it's choking); repair it with charcoal on an anvil.

items.name: Raw Uranium
items.desc: Uranium ore straight out of the ground. Feed it to a Uranium Mill to make Yellowcake.

items.name: Yellowcake
items.desc: Uranium oxide concentrate from a Uranium Mill. Six of it go into a Gas Centrifuge for one Enriched Uranium.

items.name: Enriched Uranium
items.desc: Reactor-grade uranium from a Gas Centrifuge. A Fuel Fabricator makes a Fuel Cell from one, with two Steel Ingots.

items.name: Depleted Uranium
items.desc: What the Gas Centrifuge leaves behind: dense, heavy and good at stopping radiation. A Cask Sealer uses it to shield Spent Fuel.

items.name: Spent Fuel
items.desc: A burnt-out Fuel Cell, and very much still radioactive. Carrying it gives you Radiation Sickness, worse the more you carry. Pipe it out of the reactor into storage and on to a Cask Sealer, which seals four of them into a Waste Cask.

items.name: Carbon Offset Certificate
items.desc: Right-click to retire it. It removes exactly one point of smog where you stand, and an unknowable amount of guilt. Comes in packs of four, because one would look bad.

fuelNotes: Each tick of furnace burn time gives one tick of 40 kW, and fuel only burns while the generator is supplying power. Coal runs 80 s, a coal block 800 s and a lava bucket 1000 s (the bucket stays in the slot).

guide.title: Getting Started
guide.intro: Rackcraft is about running a data centre. Racks of servers mine RackCoin, but every kilowatt they draw comes back out as heat. Mine bauxite, smelt aluminium, blast iron into steel and quartz into silicon, then build up to your first rack. Keep an eye out for abandoned data centers on the surface: fix their cut cables and they start mining for you.

guide.title: Mining RackCoin
guide.intro: Power -> racks -> RackCoin -> Crypto Exchange. Fill a Server Rack with modules, power it with Power Cable, link it to an Uplink Router with Fiber Cable, and keep its front intake below 27 C. Working racks mine RackCoin every second into one shared balance. Open a rack to see its rate or what is wrong, then spend the coin at a Crypto Exchange.

guide.title: Components
guide.intro: Every module and machine is built from the same few components. Circuit boards come first, then CPUs, RAM and GPUs.

guide.title: Compute
guide.intro: A rack has eight bays, one module each. Earnings need power of at least 50% satisfaction, a fiber link to a router, and a cool intake. Above 27 C performance falls, and at 40 C the rack stops. A rack whose power drops below 50% trips and stays off until its inlet is under 32 C.

guide.title: Power
guide.intro: Each power network draws on its sources in a fixed order: solar, wind, reactor and utility first, then batteries, then diesel. Surplus charges batteries. When power runs short, cooling and other machines are fed before racks. Battery Banks built into a solid cube (2x2x2 up to 5x5x5) become one Grid-Scale Battery, bigger and less lossy per bank.

guide.title: Fuels
guide.intro: Diesel generators are your insurance against outages, and they need fuel. Rackcraft fuels also work in vanilla furnaces.

guide.title: Cooling
guide.intro: Every kilowatt a rack draws comes back out as heat, and a rack slows down once its intake air passes 27 C and stops at 40 C. Heat leaves a rack two ways. AIR: out of the back into the room, where it spreads and slowly leaks through the walls (outdoors it blows away much faster). Keep it off the intakes with hot and cold aisles, blanking panels and raised floor, or catch it with a Rear-Door Cooler, a CRAC unit or an exhaust fan. LOOP: liquid-cooled modules (ASIC and up) send 85% of their heat down a Coolant Pipe, and Rear-Door Coolers, CRACs and reactors put heat into the same pipes. Every pipe network is one loop, and heat sinks on it take the heat out: Cooling Towers (with water from a Freshwater Pump), Dry Coolers, Chillers and Water Heat Exchangers. A loop can only take what its sinks can; any extra stays in the air. Open a rack to see how much of its heat goes to the loop and how much to the air, and check a loop with the Multimeter.

guide.title: Network & Operations
guide.intro: Connect racks over fiber to routers to sell compute. The Facility Controller tracks RackCoin and availability, runs a small parts shop, and warns you of events: outages, cooling failures, hardware failures, cable cuts, heat waves and surges.

guide.title: Storage & Autocrafting
guide.intro: Store items on drives in Storage Arrays, cold-archive them on tape, and reach it all from a Storage Terminal on the same fiber. Autocrafting runs on your server racks: they lend compute (Pi 1, 1U 2, GPU 6, Quantum 20, ASIC none, and the specialists: Crafting Coprocessor 8, Crafting Accelerator 30) and stop mining while a job runs. In the terminal, middle-click a craftable item (marked +) to order more, even when some is in stock.

guide.title: AI Contracts
guide.intro: Racks can do more than mine. Clients post contracts at the Operations Terminal: an image of something absurd, or an essay, a legal document, somebody's homework. Accept one, press Generate and pick a cluster (it needs an uplink router), and its racks work until the item reaches the required quality; finished work lands in the outbox and is delivered automatically. Pay beats mining on the same racks, more so with Tensor Accelerators, and late work earns half. Each kind of work has a lineup of models, like a real lab's: Lite models are fast and learn from a few examples but top out early, Pro models are slow and data-hungry but end up far better, and Flash sits between. Pick one per contract, or leave it on Auto for the fastest that reaches the quality. Every model trains separately, on training data: children drawing at a Kids' Art Table, and librarians shackled to Scriptorium Desks. Upload what they make to a model at the terminal and idle racks train it. Keep spare finished work: clients often order the same thing again.

guide.title: Nuclear
guide.intro: The full fuel cycle, and every machine in it is a multiblock: a solid cube of the same machine, 2x2x2 up to 5x5x5, and a serious power draw. Mine Uranium Ore deep underground; a Uranium Mill turns two Raw Uranium into a Yellowcake; a Gas Centrifuge enriches six Yellowcake into one Enriched Uranium and four Depleted Uranium; a Fuel Fabricator makes one Fuel Cell from each Enriched Uranium and two Steel Ingots; Modular Reactors burn them and leave Spent Fuel, which stops the reactor once its waste slots fill up. Spent Fuel is radioactive in your pockets: a Cask Sealer seals four of them with four Depleted Uranium into a harmless Waste Cask. Connect every cube to a Storage Array with Item Pipe and the whole cycle runs by itself.

guide.title: Creative Tools
guide.intro: Creative-only machines for building and testing. They cannot be crafted or bought at the Exchange; find them in the Rackcraft Creative tab. Right-click one to set its value in-game; only players in creative mode or operators can change it.
